- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent history, reduce forecast slope or avoid upward momentum; model tends to overreact to negative sentiment.
- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent history, model often over-optimistically forecasts upward trends; cap forecast growth or introduce early mean reversion.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >85), model frequently over-forecasts continuation; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–15% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Model consistently under-forecasts true price drops after a positive sentiment period; add a “reversion buffer” to forecast when sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to over-optimism in early days; apply a “first 7 days dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for days 1–7 if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to drift upward; introduce a “sentiment-neutral floor” rule: cap forecast at 10% below recent 18-day average if sentiment remains flat.
